scope: Reaudit actual two-batch reward construction, advantage normalization, frozen captured transitions, CPU model replay and gradient decomposition; no new training or simulation
conclusion: No verified PPO sign, mask, log-probability, action-index or update-order implementation error found. The strongest demonstrated limitation is an almost untrained state-value baseline with only sixteen independent trajectory outcomes: role-centered advantages mostly rank seed difficulty and provide very weak evidence that sampled individual actions caused better completion.

important_design_limitations.finding: The reset critic offers no state baseline in batch00, and batch01 critic predictions remain nearly constant and close to zero relative to remaining-time targets. Same-seed actions share one terminal C; global per-role centering does not distinguish intrinsic seed difficulty from action quality.

actual_evidence.relay_example: Batch01 episode8 C=53s: relay at t=1s has A=-1.1068, two relay allocations at t=34s have A=+0.5240/+0.5381. This follows remaining-time targets and does not demonstrate that later sampled helpers improved the episode.

important_design_limitations.interpretation_limit: High correlation with C is expected for a team-return estimator and is NOT proof of a biased gradient, a sign error or a causal defect. The demonstrated issue is high-variance, poorly identified credit assignment with an ineffective learned baseline.
important_design_limitations.minimal_next_check: Before further optimization, compare action quality under repeated stochastic rollouts of fixed training seeds or an independently validated state-value baseline; inspect within-seed policy improvement rather than treating faster seeds as good-action labels.

important_design_limitations.finding: Eighty decision records are only sixteen independent episode outcomes, not eighty independent completion labels. Each seed was sampled once; only nineteen Relay actions were observed, versus sixty-one Search actions. The expensive full H300 execution did not create additional policy decisions after completion.
important_design_limitations.interpretation_limit: Flattened per-decision averaging gives episodes/roles different numbers of gradient terms. This is common in episodic policy gradients and is not automatically an implementation bug: blindly dividing by decision count would itself change the estimator. Balanced episode domains do not imply equal empirical role/domain influence.

important_design_limitations.finding: Warm-started policy remains concentrated despite many legal alternatives, so a single rollout per seed explores little. Four epochs reuse the same forty records; they do not add information about unsampled alternatives.
important_design_limitations.minimal_next_check: Measure repeated-seed exploration and actual alternative-action outcomes before choosing additional optimizer steps or a larger training duration.

important_design_limitations.finding: Per-role standardization rescales policy gradients separately and removes absolute advantage scale. It does not equalize role counts: the summed loss still contains roughly three Search terms per Relay term. This is an explicit optimizer-weighting choice, not a guarantee of faithful optimization of an unweighted common-time objective.
important_design_limitations.interpretation_limit: Because every observed legal graph has only one role, the selected role is state-determined here; I did NOT find the more serious action-dependent-baseline bug that would arise if competing legal actions had different role-conditioned baselines.

important_design_limitations.finding: KL gates evaluate only the forty collected states per update. With anchor_weight=0 there is no separate frozen round17 reference constraint on unseen states. Small measured KL or one observed argmax flip cannot establish policy preservation on unseen heldout trajectories.
important_design_limitations.interpretation_limit: This is a generalization limitation rather than evidence that PPO clipping or the measured exact-KL code is wrong.

ruled_out_or_not_supported.conclusion: At a fixed decision state/time, smaller C gives a larger return. The clipped PPO loss increases the probability of sampled actions with positive A and decreases it for negative A. No sign inversion found. The +t term is a valid state/time baseline for a remaining-time return; it alone does not prove an incentive to delay.

Actual captured behavior was replayed on CPU against each frozen behavior checkpoint. Maximum logprob errors were 1.91e-6 and 4.77e-6; maximum value errors were 0 and 9.31e-10. Same masked flattened logits and temperature1 are used in collection/update. No masked or empty-action sampling defect found.

F.rrelu(...,training=self.training) does exist; any earlier claim that no RReLU exists is inaccurate. Collection and update both keep model.eval(), so this functional activation is deterministic and does not explain a behavior-logprob mismatch.

Actor/critic share AHGNN, so value loss can alter policy features. But CPU gradient decomposition at each batch's actual behavior checkpoint does NOT support critic domination: batch00 shared value gradient is zero because the value output is zero-initialized; batch01 weighted value gradient norm=0.00034749 versus policy norm=1.00900, cosine=-0.39149. Later optimizer epochs were not decomposed.

A full-horizon physical failure is assigned C=300 by the metric and is not filtered merely for success=False; collection rejects incomplete/runtime-error episodes and the updater requires every scheduled collector to succeed technically. No success-only filtering was found. Actual sixteen training episodes happened to be safe/successful, so there were no observed failure examples.

Behavior is frozen throughout each collection batch and replayed before updates; critic output/Adam reset only once; second batch loads prior optimizer state. Existing on-policy/update checks address mechanical consistency, not effectiveness of the learning signal.

verification.sampling_variance_causality_warning: The observed statistics identify weak data/credit assignment, not a proven cause of the heldout regression.
